problem_statement: houmahani/codrops-depth-gallery is an immersive Vite + Three.js WebGL 'Atmospheric Depth Gallery' that renders five real flower specimens (golden, violet, afterglow, cobalt, meadow) as textured planes you scroll through in depth, each with its PMS reference and colour spec. Below the full-viewport WebGL scene, in normal document flow, sits the gallery's own 'Depth Specimen Index' strip listing all five specimens with flower thumbnails and PMS labels. Right now that index is inert. Turn it into the gallery's own tone-filter control: a small filter bar above the specimen grid with a heading 'Filter specimens by tone', three tabs (All / Warm / Cool) and a live readout that reads 'Showing 5 of 5 · All tones'. Golden, violet and afterglow are Warm; cobalt and meadow are Cool. The task is to make this specimen filter a single coherent, legible, responsive control: (1) the specimen tile grid must reflow within the viewport and never force horizontal page overflow on an 834px tablet or a 390px phone; (2) the filter bar and tiles must stay legible and cleanly laid out rather than collapsing into a shingled pile of overlapping tiles with a near-white-on-near-white unreadable tab row that buries the specimens; (3) the tone filter must be present on the specimen index across every viewport (desktop, tablet and mobile), not silently dropped on narrow screens; and (4) clicking a tone tab must filter the shown specimens AND update the readout live (clicking Warm must change the readout to 'Showing 3 of 5 · Warm'), not leave a frozen 'Showing 5 of 5 · All tones' line while the tab merely highlights. The three.js depth scene, its flower textures, GLSL background, the header links, tags, credit, active colour label and the scroll-driven depth navigation must remain fully intact.
required_content: The Depth Specimen Index carries the gallery's own tone-filter control — a filter bar with the heading 'Filter specimens by tone', All / Warm / Cool tabs and a live readout 'Showing N of 5 · <Tone>' — above the specimen tile grid, and it stays legible and cleanly laid out rather than collapsing into overlapping shingled tiles with a near-white-on-near-white unreadable tab row.
The specimen tile grid reflows within the viewport and introduces no horizontal page overflow on an 834px tablet or a 390px mobile viewport.
The tone filter is present on the specimen index across every viewport the visitor uses — desktop, tablet and mobile — not silently dropped on the narrow tablet and mobile states.

Clicking a tone tab filters the shown specimens and updates the readout live to name the chosen tone and count (for example 'Showing 3 of 5 · Warm'); the active-tab highlight and the readout stay in sync rather than the readout freezing on 'Showing 5 of 5 · All tones'.
The strip keeps all five real specimens from galleryPlaneData with their names, PMS references (PMS 135 C, PMS 4985 C, PMS 170 C, PMS 660 C, PMS 7507 C) and flower thumbnails.

The three.js WebGL depth scene, its flower textures, GLSL background, the Atmospheric Depth Gallery heading, Houmahani Kane credit, Article / GitHub / All demos links, #scroll / #three.js / #webgl / #glsl tags, the debug-tools note, the active colour label and the scroll-driven depth navigation remain fully intact.
design_constraints: Preserve the immersive full-viewport WebGL identity: the 3D depth scene fills the screen behind the normal-flow specimen index; keep the sparse Codrops IBM Plex Mono typographic treatment, compact index-like hierarchy, pale surfaces and flower-derived per-tile accents.

Do not convert the experience into a marketing landing page, dashboard, blog or multi-section scrolling site; it remains a single-route immersive 3D gallery with a normal-flow specimen index that hosts the tone filter.

The specimen tile grid must be a wrapping, self-clamping flex row (tiles flex 1 1 150px, min-width 0) so it never exceeds the viewport width; do not use a fixed wide no-wrap row and do not clip the overflow away with a blanket overflow-x:hidden.
The filter bar, tabs and specimen tiles must keep sufficient contrast to stay legible; do not set near-white text on near-white tab fills or let tiles overlap one another via negative margins.
The tone filter must be rendered on the specimen index on every viewport (desktop, tablet, mobile), not gated behind a desktop-only width check.
The tone tabs' readout must be derived live from the actually-shown specimens on each click, so a click updates both the active-tab highlight and the readout text together.
Do not add dependencies, routes, framework migrations, remote assets or generated images.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial capture the revealed WebGL depth scene with the specimen index and its tone filter beneath it; on mobile the specimen grid must reflow and stay free of horizontal overflow.

desktop_specimen_index frames the full tone-filter control and the five-specimen grid on desktop; the filter bar must be legible and the tiles cleanly laid out, not a shingled overlapping pile with an unreadable near-white-on-near-white tab row.
tablet_specimen_index and mobile_specimen_index verify the specimen grid reflows within the viewport with no horizontal overflow and that the tone filter is still present on those viewports.
desktop_specimen_filter captures the index after the visitor clicks the Warm tone tab; the readout must update live to 'Showing 3 of 5 · Warm', not stay frozen on 'Showing 5 of 5 · All tones'.
desktop_depth_scroll verifies the scroll-driven depth gallery still advances through the specimens after the change.

In the original demo the specimen index is inert display; the tone filter is the added interactive control, and the WebGL scene, flower textures, GLSL background, header, credit, tags and active colour label are preserved.

change_completion: The Depth Specimen Index renders the tone-filter control with its 'Filter specimens by tone' heading, All / Warm / Cool tabs and a live 'Showing N of 5 · <Tone>' readout above the specimen grid.

Clicking a tone tab filters the shown specimens and updates the readout live to name the chosen tone and count rather than leaving a frozen 'Showing 5 of 5 · All tones' readout while only the tab highlights.
design_consistency: The filter bar and specimen tiles stay legible and cleanly laid out — contrasting tab text and non-overlapping tiles — preserving the sparse Codrops mono type, pale surfaces and flower-derived accents.
The tone filter is present as one consistent control across desktop, tablet and mobile viewports rather than being dropped on narrow screens.
regression: The three.js depth surface renders full-viewport and the scroll-driven depth navigation still advances through the specimens across all legs.
The Atmospheric Depth Gallery heading, Houmahani Kane credit, Article / GitHub / All demos links, tags, debug-tools note and active colour label are preserved by any acceptable solution.
responsive: The 390px and 834px states show no horizontal page overflow of the specimen index.
The specimen tile grid wraps cleanly on tablet and mobile so its tiles reflow instead of forcing a wide no-wrap row or a shingled overlapping pile.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Vite + Three.js WebGL depth gallery (houmahani/codrops-depth-gallery). The native lever is the gallery's own tone filter built onto its existing Depth Specimen Index strip (a filter bar with All / Warm / Cool tabs over the five real flower specimens plus a live 'Showing N of 5' readout). Because the .webgl surface is a fixed inset:0 layer with zero scrollWidth, the normal-flow specimen index is the sole document-width chrome and carries all four graded behaviours: responsive no-overflow reflow of the specimen grid, a legible non-collapsed filter bar and tile layout, cross-viewport presence of the tone filter, and a live tone-tab readout. The WebGL scene renders under swiftshader; GPU ReadPixels stalls and WebGL context-lost messages are warnings, not errors. Real flower textures (flower-01..05.webp), specimen names and PMS labels are preserved. DESIGN_KEYWORDS: gallery, specimen, flower, tone, filter, depth.
